title: A land whose process died leaves the item's run state at landing, and kbmon's landing queue lists it as waiting for a lock nobody holds
goal: kbmon's landing queue lists only the items whose land process runs, in the order the lock will take them, so a land that died leaves no queue entry that peers read as a held lock or a waiter

run:
import os
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bl_clean
import bl_close
import mon_host
import mon_sessions

root = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
subprocess.run(["git", "init", "-q", str(root)], check=True)
lock = bl_close.landing_lock_path(root)
lock.write_text(f"pid={os.getpid()}\nclone={root}\nstarted=2026-11-09T00:00:00Z\nitem=ST-aaaaaaaa\n", encoding="utf-8")
# the run state of ST-bbbbbbbb is landing, but no live process record of it exists: its land died
mon_sessions.run_states = lambda ctx: {"ST-aaaaaaaa": "landing", "ST-bbbbbbbb": "landing"}
mon_sessions.backlog = lambda r: None
mon_sessions.landing_steps = lambda r: {}
bl_clean.coord_state = lambda *a, **k: {"owners": []}
out = mon_host.land_lock(types.SimpleNamespace(root=root))
queue = [q["id"] for q in out["queue"]]
print("landing queue shown to peers:", queue)
sys.exit(0 if "ST-bbbbbbbb" not in queue else 1)
